subject: Connection behavior & fallback routing — short-term workaround + roadmap ask
messages:
From: Cara Nguyen <cara@storix.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@storix.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: (URGENT) Intermittent 503s and generation differences during fallbacks

Marcus — thanks again for the call this morning. We started seeing a spike of 503s around 08:50 PST and when the system fell back to the smaller variant the responses were not matching the golden prompts we validated against (different formatting, truncated lists). Attached is a short log snippet showing the 503s and a capture of two consecutive requests where the first used the primary model and the second used the fallback. Can you confirm whether the fallback model should be pinned to the same tokenizer/config? Our legal/ops team is worried about inconsistent outputs during live demos.

Storage of the logs is here: <link in ops mailbox> — I pasted a couple lines below.

[attachment: storix-500-log-snippet.txt]

Example (redacted):
- 2027-09-13T08:50:12Z inbound request id=abc123 -> 200 model=rl-encoder-v2
- 2027-09-13T08:50:14Z inbound request id=abc124 -> 503 -> fallback model=rl-encoder-v2-compact -> response truncated

Short ask: can Redwood provide a short-term mitigation so fallbacks preserve canonical formatting, and a longer-term plan so variant fallbacks are surfaced and pinned when a customer requests? We’re demoing to the exec team Wednesday.

Thanks,
Cara Nguyen
Head of Integrations, Storix
cara@storix.com

Cara — I’m on it. Appreciate the logs; that makes repro much faster. Quick answers up front:
- Short-term: we can enable a routing policy that prefers model variants with identical tokenizer/formatting characteristics for your production routes. That’s a config flip for Dedicated/Private and a policy change on Hosted when you have org-level pinning.
- Immediate mitigation: I’ll request a temporary rule to prevent automatic fallback to the compact variant for Storix’s route until we ship a safer fallback behavior.

I need engineering to confirm feasibility and time. Looping in Dev (runtime) and Logan (product) to confirm the risk/scope and provide an ETA. For the demo on Wed I’ll ask for an emergency runbook if we can’t guarantee full pinning by then.

Action for Storix: if you can share the two example payloads (original request + fallback response) as redacted JSON that will speed up repro.

—Marcus

Subject: Fwd: (URGENT) Intermittent 503s and generation differences during fallbacks — customer impact and short-term ask

Team — forwarding Storix thread. TL;DR: customer saw a 503 and automatic fallback to a compact variant which produced format/truncation differences. They need short-term mitigation (prevent compact fallback) for their production route and longer-term: an explicit fallback contract/policy that can be requested per route (pin fallback model family and enforce tokenizer compatibility).

Key asks:
- Can runtime set a temporary route-level override to disallow compact variants as fallback for route id=storix-prod-01?
- If runtime cannot quickly flip this for hosted routes, can we implement an outbound gating rule that forces 429 (or queue) instead of fallback for pinned routes?
- Product: if we introduce a "fallback contract" flag, what are the implications for capacity and SLOs? Is there an acceptable default behavior?

Customer demo Wed 09/15 EOD PST — ideally have something low-risk by then (config flip or runbook). If we need a cross-team rollback/fallback, I want to be explicit about who owns the runbook. Lauren: can you greenlight an exec escalation if we need a capacity exception? Logan: need your tradeoff guidance for roadmap prioritization — is this something we can treat as critical for Hosted?

Quoted for context:
> On Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700 Cara Nguyen <cara@storix.com> wrote:
> > Marcus — thanks again for the call this morning. We started seeing a spike of 503s...

—Marcus

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: (URGENT) Intermittent 503s and generation differences during fallbacks — customer impact and short-term ask

Thanks for the ping. Quick technical summary after an initial triage of the logs Marcus attached:
1) The 503s align with an autoscaler preemption on the primary pool (short spike). The request routing policy currently picks the first compatible variant it finds. The compact variant uses a different tokenizer config and an aggressive max_tokens clamp which explains truncated bullets.
2) Short-term mitigation options (feasible in the next 24–48 hours):
   - Route override: we can add a route-level "fallback_whitelist" that lists allowed fallback families. For Storix I can add rl-encoder-v2-family only. This is a config change; no code deploy and low risk.
   - Fallback gating: return 503->queue/429 instead of auto-fallback for pinned routes. That requires a small change in the routing layer (feature flag toggle) and a short deploy — ~1 week safe path, but could be hotfixed faster with exec signoff.
   - Tokenizer normalization: normalize outgoing tokens between compatible variants by applying a canonical post-processor. This is more invasive and should be on the roadmap.

3) Longer term: I agree a "fallback contract" concept (route-level policy + telemetry) makes sense. Product questions: do we want the contract to be an explicit opt-in with capacity reservation (reserved capacity for backup variants) or opt-out with best-effort? Opt-in with reservation adds cost but is the only way to guarantee exact parity.

Proposed immediate plan:
- I will push a route override for storix-prod-01 today to ban compact variants.
- Create JIRA-RT-9134 to track the fallback-contract epic and link to a Drive proposal (I also attached a one-pager).
- Share an emergency runbook that SEs can use during the demo to manually divert traffic to a reserved pool if needed.

Attachments: fallback-routing-proposal.pdf (proposal), runbook-draft.md (initial runbook snippet)

Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
